name: Tukulor Empire
alt: Empire of El Hadj Umar Tall

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Tamba
predecessors.text: Dinguiraye, founded 1851 in the Kingdom of Tamba

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: the empire's last land: Bandiagara/Massina (April 1893) and the residual Dinguiraye and Bambuk holdings

ledger.x: 1852: Umar Tall defeats King Yambi of Tamba and founds his jihad state around Dinguiraye.
1855: Umar Tall seizes Kaarta from the Bambara.
1855: the seat moves to Nioro du Sahel.
1860: Umar Tall invades the Bambara kingdom of Ségou.
10 March 1861: Ségou falls to Umar Tall.
1861: Umar Tall takes Ségou and makes it his capital.
1861: the capital moves from Nioro to Ségou.
1862: Umar Tall attacks the Fulbe Massina state.
May 1862: Djenné falls, then Hamdullahi, the Massina capital.
February 1864: Massina rebels retake Hamdullahi and Umar Tall is killed (14 February, Degembere); his son Ahmadu succeeds.
1884: Ahmadu moves his court to Nioro after Muntaga's revolt.
1891: the French take Nioro and Kaarta.
29 April 1893: Bandiagara falls and the French install Aguibou as puppet ruler of Massina on 4 May.

wars.name: Umar Tall's jihad: Tamba, Bambuk and Kaarta
wars.outcome: Tukulor victories: Tamba (September 1852), Bambuk (1854), Nioro and Kaarta (April 1855).

wars.name: Siege of Medina Fort
wars.outcome: The siege failed on 18 July 1857 when Faidherbe arrived with relief forces; the 1860 treaty then recognised Umar's sphere in Futa Toro and assigned Kaarta and Segu to his followers.

wars.name: Umar Tall's conquest of Ségou and Massina
wars.outcome: Nyamina 25 May 1860, Witala September 1860, Ségou 10 March 1861, Djenné and Hamdullahi May 1862.

wars.name: Massina revolt
wars.outcome: Rebels besieged Umar Tall at Hamdullahi, captured it in February 1864 and Umar was killed; Tidiani Tall contested the succession from Bandiagara.

wars.name: Revolt of Muntaga
wars.outcome: Ahmadu besieged Nioro; Muntaga blew up his powder magazine rather than surrender.

certainty.note: Pages give no outline; the empire was a string of garrisons and provinces run by Umar's relatives.
